question_text: Module 9 opens by explaining how belonging to God's family works. According to the introduction, how does a person come to belong?
answer_options: We earn belonging by being good enough for the group
We grow spiritually first, and belonging follows our maturity
God adopts us into His family first, and then we grow
We belong once church leaders formally approve our membership
correct_answer: God adopts us into His family first, and then we grow

question_text: The module uses the illustration of a child adopted into a loving home who is given the family name, handed a chair, and told 'you are ours now.' What is this illustration teaching?
answer_options: You do not belong because you performed; you belong because God chose you
Adopted children must work hard to keep their place at the table
God's family accepts only those who first prove themselves faithful
Belonging comes gradually as you learn the family's rules
correct_answer: You do not belong because you performed; you belong because God chose you

question_text: The module names one relationship as the most important of all. Which relationship is it, and why?
answer_options: Relationship with others, because love is the greatest commandment
Relationship with self, because you cannot love others until you love yourself
Relationship with church leaders, because they watch over your soul
Relationship with God, because every other relationship grows healthier when it is right
correct_answer: Relationship with God, because every other relationship grows healthier when it is right

question_text: Under 'How to Grow Closer to God', the module lists five practices. Which option matches the list given in the lesson?
answer_options: Fast weekly, attend every service, memorise creeds, keep vigils, and tithe
Talk to Him in prayer, listen by reading His Word, walk with the Holy Spirit daily, worship wholeheartedly, and trust and obey what He says
Study theology, join a ministry, take mission trips, mentor others, and journal
Confess daily, avoid unbelievers, wear modest clothing, sing hymns, and rest on the Sabbath
correct_answer: Talk to Him in prayer, listen by reading His Word, walk with the Holy Spirit daily, worship wholeheartedly, and trust and obey what He says

question_text: On the relationship with self, the module says how you see yourself, treat yourself, and think of yourself should be influenced by one thing only. What is it?
answer_options: Your past record, which keeps you humble about who you really are
The honest opinions of the people who know you best
Your achievements and growth since becoming a believer
God's standpoint pertaining to you — your new creation identity in Christ
correct_answer: God's standpoint pertaining to you — your new creation identity in Christ

question_text: The module says that regardless of your past, you should be able to forgive yourself. What reason does it give, and what does it call the refusal to do so?
answer_options: Because God has forgiven you — and not being able to forgive yourself is a sense of pride
Because time heals all wounds — and refusing to move on is a sign of weakness
Because everyone makes mistakes — and dwelling on them is simply unproductive
Because your good works now outweigh the past — and doubting that is unbelief
correct_answer: Because God has forgiven you — and not being able to forgive yourself is a sense of pride

question_text: Quoting Romans 8:38-39 under 'You Are Deeply Loved', what conclusion does the module draw for how you relate to yourself?
answer_options: God's love must be maintained by daily devotion, so guard it carefully
God loves you when you love others, so serve people to stay loved
Nothing in all creation can separate you from God's love, so you can love yourself, seeing yourself as He sees you
God's love covers the past only, so present failures must still be paid for
correct_answer: Nothing in all creation can separate you from God's love, so you can love yourself, seeing yourself as He sees you

question_text: From John 13:34-35, the module states how the world will know that we are disciples of Jesus. What is the mark it names?
answer_options: Our bold public preaching of the gospel
Our love for one another, not how much we know
Our separation from worldly patterns and habits
Our faithful attendance at church gatherings
correct_answer: Our love for one another, not how much we know

question_text: The module twice uses the picture of a burning coal — pulled from the fire it grows cold; kept with the others it stays burning. What truth is this illustrating?
answer_options: Believers were never meant to stay warm alone; planted together in community, we keep each other burning
Zeal naturally fades with age, so young believers must be especially fervent
Trials are the fire God uses to refine each believer individually
A believer who falls away can never be restored to their first fire
correct_answer: Believers were never meant to stay warm alone; planted together in community, we keep each other burning

question_text: 'The Family Table' answers the question 'why the local church?' with five reasons the church matters. Which option lists all five as taught?
answer_options: Worship, prayer, evangelism, giving, and service
Preaching, healing, deliverance, communion, and missions
Fellowship, leadership, tradition, sacraments, and discipline
Community, doctrine, covering, the ordinances, and growth
correct_answer: Community, doctrine, covering, the ordinances, and growth
